statuses.guaranteed: Deterministic and blocking. Implemented, and a behavioural test proves it.
statuses.advisory: Projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours it is not observable from outside. Documentation, not enforcement.
statuses.planned: Specified and not implemented. Named so the omission is visible.
statuses.rejected: Considered and deliberately refused, with the reason recorded.

claims.claim: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key
claims.note: A restricted YAML subset. Tabs, anchors, flow maps and multi-line scalars are refused rather than guessed at.

claims.claim: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist
Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
claims.note: The path must exist, be executable, and be invoked by the named dispatcher. A hook that invokes it and discards the exit code counts as not wired.

claims.claim: Exit codes are a contract, and no code means "warn and continue"
Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
claims.note: Running update twice leaves the byte-identical file. The test asserts the hash.

claims.claim: Every generated instruction file is fingerprinted, and a hand edit is detected
A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
claims.note: How a repository that already has a hand-written CLAUDE.md adopts Majordomus. An edit outside the markers is never drift; an edit inside them is caught. Malformed markers are refused, not guessed at.

claims.claim: Wiring is found in a hook or in any subhook of the directory that hook dispatches to
claims.note: The finding names the file that actually carries the invocation. A subhook that is not executable is reported as not wired, because the dispatcher skips it.

claims.claim: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
claims.note: update refuses, offers a diff, and overwrites only under an explicit flag.

claims.claim: The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check
claims.note: Over budget, nothing is written at all.

claims.claim: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve
A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
Installing into a repository that already has an installation is refused
Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
Nothing performs a network call, evaluates generated text, or deletes recursively
A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
claims.note: A scope path that escapes the repository root is refused. Starting a second task while one is active is refused.

claims.claim: Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored
claims.note: A handover body that tries to set one is rejected rather than merged.

claims.claim: check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now
A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
State read back is labelled exact, advanced, diverged or different_context against git
Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
claims.note: Reported, never blocking. Work in progress is reported and never blocked.

claims.claim: watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift
handover writes an append-only record with computed front matter and required sections
claims.note: A body with a missing or empty required section is refused and names the sections.

claims.claim: Handovers carry durable facts, never conversation transcripts
finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet
An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
claims.note: no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist. failed means the work could not be done. They are different facts.

claims.claim: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
claims.note: The axes are validated and projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours them is not observable from outside the worker.

claims.claim: A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model
claims.note: Mapping a class to a concrete model is left to whoever runs the worker. Majordomus never selects or invokes a model.

claims.claim: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more
claims.note: check --explain prints the context toggles for the active profile. Nothing measures what the worker actually read.

claims.claim: Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed
A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported
claims.note: The staleness report is guaranteed. Whether the worker checkpoints is not.

claims.claim: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
claims.note: v0.2. The one implementation studied was rolled back within days because its limits were global constants rather than task-derived.

claims.claim: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
claims.note: v0.3. Nothing in v0.1 measures token spend. Any estimated_ field is labelled and excluded from enforcement.

claims.claim: Cost per accepted outcome will be reported from measured data only
Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
claims.note: v0.5. Recommendations only. Majordomus does not invoke a model.

claims.claim: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers
Dependencies between tasks are deliberately not represented
claims.note: No use case in the evidence justified a dependency graph. Listed so that the omission is visible rather than assumed to be an oversight. Revisited only when a real case appears.
